_comment: Registration for scripts/check-control-ci-deps.py (issue #1036).
WHY THIS GATE NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): it is a gate that lets work
THROUGH. `make verify` reads its green as 'no registered control needs a binary
the battery's CI step lacks', and nothing downstream re-derives that.
AND IT IS THE HARDEST KIND TO NOTICE GOING BLIND, which is the real argument
for these cases. Every surface it judges belongs to an environment it is not
running in: the dev box has git, jq, shellcheck and gitleaks, so a version of
this gate that checked NOTHING would print the same green here, forever, and
the first evidence of the blindness would be the CI red it exists to prevent -
which is precisely the sequence that produced this issue.
THE CASES ARE WHOLE FIXTURE TREES, not the real repository. The gate takes
--root, so a case is a miniature repo: a two-step .woodpecker.yml, one
controls/toy/control.json, and one scripts/toy-gate.sh. Deliberately tiny -
the question is whether the gate can tell a runnable control from one that
would take the register down.
TWO BAD CASES, because the gate draws two distinctions and they fail in
different directions:
bad-missing-binary  a control whose GATE hard-requires `git`, while its
invocation (`sh`) is entirely unremarkable. This is the
real failure's shape: the control that took the whole
battery down declared nothing unusual either. A gate
that read only the invocation scores this clean, and
the committed anchor does exactly that.
bad-stale-image     the pipeline runs an image the recorded contents list
does not describe. Every answer about what is provided
is then about a container that no longer runs the
battery, so the honest verdict is UNKNOWN. Without this
case the pin could rot silently and the gate would keep
reporting confident greens against a retired image -
the hand-maintained-number failure one level up from
the one this gate catches.
THE GOOD CASE IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS for a gate wedged at 'fail': a check
that refuses every tree passes both bad cases on its own, and this gate is in
`make verify`, so a false red blocks every merge in the repository.
Stdlib-only and git-free, like the gate: no binary this fixture needs is
absent from the slim CI image, so the control gives the same verdict there as
here. That property is not incidental - a control for a gate ABOUT CI
dependencies that itself needed a binary CI lacks would be this issue's own
defect, one level further in.

cases.name: bad-missing-binary
cases.why: The toy gate hard-requires `git`, which the derived CI set does not provide. If this scores GOOD the gate cannot see the dependency shape that actually took the register down - one carried by the gate script, not by the invocation.

cases.name: bad-stale-image
cases.why: The pipeline's battery step runs an image the recorded contents list does not describe. If this scores GOOD the provided-binary set can silently describe a retired container while the gate keeps reporting confident greens against it.

cases.name: good-all-present
cases.why: A tree whose one control needs only `sh`, which the image provides, and whose pipeline runs the pinned image. THE HALF THAT MATTERS for a gate wedged at 'fail': a check that refuses every tree is indistinguishable from a working one on the bad cases alone, and this gate sits in `make verify`, so a false red blocks every merge.

cases.name: bad-wrapper-without-provided-key
cases.why: A control whose gate hard-requires curl, invoked through a wrapper that stages a real curl stub, but which declares no `ci_deps_provided_by_invocation`. Today's real make-test failure (lane-serveability-check, issue #1407 fallout), reproduced as the intended red: the checker must not trust a wrapper's own stub without an explicit, verified claim.

cases.name: good-wrapper-with-verified-provided-key
cases.why: Identical to bad-wrapper-without-provided-key except the control declares `ci_deps_provided_by_invocation: ["curl"]`, and the wrapper's own text genuinely demonstrates it. The half that matters for a gate wedged at 'fail': a checker that refuses every provided claim passes the bad cases on its own.

cases.name: bad-wrapper-provided-key-not-created
cases.why: The control claims `ci_deps_provided_by_invocation: ["curl"]`, but its wrapper stages a stub named `wget`, never `curl`. A checker that trusted the declared key as free text would score this clean; it must verify the claim against the wrapper's own text and refuse a stale one.

cases.name: bad-wrapper-gate-needs-not-provided
cases.why: The gate hard-requires both curl and jq; the wrapper genuinely stages and the control genuinely (and correctly) claims only curl. jq must still be reported as needed - pinning that `ci_deps_provided_by_invocation` narrows a gate's needs by exactly what it verifies, never by walking the wrapper INSTEAD of the gate (the orchestrator's ruled-out direction, which would drop every binary the gate needs that a wrapper happens not to stub, across the 26 registered controls that invoke one).

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: the gate is new and never shipped blind, so there is no revision to vendor - `--verify-provenance` therefore reports `unverified`, which is correct and must never be read as `ok`. This is the FIRST FRAMING, on the record: the issue asked for 'a tripwire checking each registered control's declared invocation ... against the binaries the CI image actually provides', and written straight from that sentence you get this file. It reads invocation[0] and stops, so it misses bad-missing-binary (the dependency is in the gate script) and bad-stale-image (it never checks the pin), and agrees with the real gate on good-all-present, which is what makes the demonstration isolated.

limits: SINCE #1168 A PYTHON GATE'S MODULE-LEVEL IMPORTS ARE EXAMINED TOO, and `bad-python-import` is that case: a toy gate importing `pydantic` on load, which the battery's image does not provide, so the battery - which refuses to skip a control it cannot run - would be taken down by this one registration. The constructed anchor misses it for the same reason it misses the binary case: it reads `invocation[0]` and stops, and `invocation[0]` here is `python3`, which the image HAS. `good-python-stdlib-only` is the guard rail, because "flag a python gate whose imports the image lacks" is satisfiable by flagging every python gate - which would red 26 of this repository's 41 controls. THE WALK IS MODULE-LEVEL ONLY and that is a bound, not a shortcut: an import inside a function is conditional on a call path this reader cannot decide, and #1163 deliberately created seven such imports in `lib/cicd/cli.py` that the gate's own path never takes - following them would report a requirement that is false. Deferred imports are COUNTED in the success line instead. NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT: a green here does not mean a control RUNS in the image, which `make negative-controls-image` answers by running it there. THE `if TYPE_CHECKING:` PAIR (#1162) BOUNDS THE ONE EXEMPTION THIS WALK MAKES. `good-python-type-checking-only` is a gate whose only pydantic import sits under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`, which is False by definition at runtime, so the gate loads in an image without pydantic and the check must NOT report it. The walk got that wrong and said the import 'runs on load' about code that does not run, which blocked a ratified change - an over-approximating check states a claim its input does not support, and that is the same contract violation as an under-approximating one. `bad-python-import-under-if-true` is its negative membership: the exemption is matched as a LITERAL name, never by evaluating the condition, so a block that looks just as constant must still report. The two are a pair; either alone would let the exemption widen into 'any if' with nothing objecting. The first cut of the fix also deferred the whole `ast.If` including its `else:`, silently exempting an import that does run, which is why only the `if` body is deferred now.
